• Nonpurchase: (91/100)/(68/75) = 273/272.

273⁸¹⁷ ≥ 20 × 272⁸¹⁷

from fractions import Fraction

P0 = Fraction(7, 75)
Q = Fraction(1, 10)
THRESHOLD = Fraction(20)


def monitor(outcomes):
    try:
        iterator = iter(outcomes)
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise ValueError("Expected an iterable of integer zeros and ones") from exc

    assignments = 0
    purchases = 0
    process = Fraction(1)
    first_crossing = None

    while True:
        # Choose using previous outcomes only, before fetching this outcome.
        q = Q if 75 * purchases > 7 * assignments else P0

        try:
            x = next(iterator)
        except StopIteration:
            return first_crossing

        if isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError("Outcomes must be integer 0 or 1, not Booleans")

        multiplier = q / P0 if x == 1 else (1 - q) / (1 - P0)
        process *= multiplier
        assignments += 1
        purchases += x

        if first_crossing is None and process >= THRESHOLD:
            first_crossing = assignments


def _ones_then_invalid():
    yield from (1 for _ in range(100))
    yield True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Exact verification of the invalid rule's sharp bound.
    assert Fraction(273, 272) ** 816 < THRESHOLD
    assert Fraction(273, 272) ** 817 >= THRESHOLD

    assert monitor(iter(())) is None
    assert monitor(0 for _ in range(1000)) is None
    assert monitor(1 for _ in range(100)) == 45

    # Validation continues after the crossing at index 45.
    try:
        monitor(_ones_then_invalid())
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Expected ValueError after crossing")

    print("All tests passed")

cells.question: Switch to Euclidean geometry. For an integer dimension d at least three, consider d plus one labeled points. Every pairwise squared distance equals one except the squared distance between points zero and one, which equals t. Derive the exact range of t permitting a nondegenerate simplex in d-dimensional Euclidean space, and its squared volume as a function of d and t. Prove necessity and sufficiency using a Gram matrix, not merely triangle inequalities. At both endpoints, determine the affine dimension and explain which points coincide, if any.

cells.answer:
The exact range for a nondegenerate simplex is
\[
0<t<\frac{2d}{d-1},
\]
and its squared volume is
\[
V_d^2=\frac{t\bigl(2d-(d-1)t\bigr)}{2^d(d!)^2}.
\]

To prove this, take point zero as the origin and write v_i=p_i-p_0 for i=1,…,d. The distance identity gives the Gram matrix
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}
t & \frac t2\mathbf1^T\\
\frac t2\mathbf1 & B
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\frac12(I_{d-1}+\mathbf1\mathbf1^T).
\]
Indeed, v_1 has squared norm t, the other vectors have squared norm one, their mutual inner products are one-half, and v_1’s inner product with each is t/2.

The matrix B is positive definite: its eigenvalues are d/2 in the all-ones direction and 1/2 in the other d−2 directions. Thus
\[
\mathbf1^TB^{-1}\mathbf1=\frac{2(d-1)}d.
\]
By the Schur complement, G is positive definite exactly when
\[
t-\frac{t^2}{4}\frac{2(d-1)}d
=\frac{t\bigl(2d-(d-1)t\bigr)}{2d}>0.
\]
This proves necessity. It also proves sufficiency: every positive-definite d-by-d Gram matrix is realized by d linearly independent vectors in Euclidean d-space, and these entries reproduce every specified distance.

For the volume,
\[
\det B=\frac d{2^{d-1}},\qquad
\det G=\frac{t\bigl(2d-(d-1)t\bigr)}{2^d}.
\]
Since a simplex’s squared volume is det(G)/(d!)², this gives the stated formula.

At either endpoint G is positive semidefinite with rank d−1, so the affine dimension is exactly d−1:

• At t=0, points zero and one coincide. The remaining distinct points, together with that common point, form a regular (d−1)-simplex. No other points coincide.

• At t=2d/(d−1), no points coincide because every pairwise distance is positive. The null-vector relation is
\[
v_1=\frac{2}{d-1}\sum_{j=2}^d v_j,
\]
so
\[
\frac{p_0+p_1}{2}=\frac1{d-1}\sum_{j=2}^d p_j.
\]
Thus the midpoint of points zero and one is the centroid of the other d−1 points.

A nondegenerate simplex exists exactly when

Its squared d-dimensional volume is

V² = t[2d − (d−1)t] / [2^d(d!)²].

To prove this, place point zero at the origin and let vᵢ = pᵢ − p₀ for i = 1,…,d. The distance identity gives the Gram matrix

G = [ t          (t/2)1ᵀ ]
    [ (t/2)1     B       ],

where B = (I + J)/2 has size d−1, and J is the all-ones matrix. Its eigenvalues are d/2 along the all-ones vector and 1/2 in the orthogonal directions. Thus B is positive definite, det B = d/2^(d−1), and 1ᵀB⁻¹1 = 2(d−1)/d.

Consequently, G is positive definite exactly when its Schur complement is positive:

t − (t²/4)1ᵀB⁻¹1 = t[1 − (d−1)t/(2d)] > 0.

This yields precisely the stated open interval. Necessity follows because a nondegenerate Euclidean simplex has a positive-definite Gram matrix. For sufficiency, any such positive-definite G can be factored as G = XᵀX; its columns give d independent vectors in Euclidean d-space with exactly the required distances.

The same calculation gives

det G = det B · t[1 − (d−1)t/(2d)]
      = t[2d − (d−1)t]/2^d.

Since V² = det G/(d!)², this proves the volume formula.

At both endpoints, G is positive semidefinite with rank d−1, so the affine dimension is exactly d−1 and the d-dimensional volume is zero.

• At t = 0, points zero and one coincide. Together with points two through d, the distinct points form a regular (d−1)-simplex of side length one. No other points coincide.

• At t = 2d/(d−1), no points coincide, because every pairwise squared distance is positive. The zero Schur complement gives v₁ = [2/(d−1)]∑ᵢ₌₂ᵈvᵢ, equivalently

(p₀ + p₁)/2 = (p₂ + ⋯ + p_d)/(d−1).

Outside the closed interval, the Schur complement is negative, so the Gram matrix is not positive semidefinite and no Euclidean realization exists.

class WitnessDAG:
    # Node: (start, end, length, left, right, edge_id).
    # Empty node: length=0, no children or edge ID.
    # Leaf: length=1, original input edge ID.
    # Internal node: concatenate left then right.
    def __init__(self):
        self.nodes = []
        self.root = None

    def edge_at(self, i):
        """Return edge ID at zero-based position i, without expansion."""
        if (not isinstance(i, int) or isinstance(i, bool)
                or not 0 <= i < self.nodes[self.root][2]):
            raise IndexError('edge index out of range')
        node = self.root
        while True:
            _, _, _, left, right, eid = self.nodes[node]
            if eid is not None:
                return eid
            left_length = self.nodes[left][2]
            if i < left_length:
                node = left
            else:
                i -= left_length
                node = right


def classify_root(N, edges, S, T, L):
    """Minimum-cost walk using exactly L edges.

    Return ('finite', integer_cost, WitnessDAG), or
           ('unreachable', None, None).
    Edge IDs are zero-based positions in the input iterable.
    Invalid input raises ValueError.
    """
    def integer(x):
        return isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool)

    if not integer(N) or not 1 <= N <= 60:
        raise ValueError('require 1 <= N <= 60')
    if not (integer(S) and integer(T)
            and 0 <= S < N and 0 <= T < N):
        raise ValueError('invalid endpoints')
    if not integer(L) or not 0 <= L <= 10**18:
        raise ValueError('require 0 <= L <= 10**18')

    E = []
    try:
        iterator = iter(edges)
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise ValueError('edges must be iterable') from exc
    for edge in iterator:
        if len(E) >= 10000:
            raise ValueError('too many edges')
        try:
            u, v, w = edge
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise ValueError('expected (u, v, w)') from exc
        if not (integer(u) and integer(v) and integer(w)
                and 0 <= u < N and 0 <= v < N
                and abs(w) <= 10**12):
            raise ValueError('invalid edge')
        E.append((u, v, w))

    dag = WitnessDAG()

    def matrix():
        return [[None] * N for _ in range(N)]

    def add_node(u, v, length, left=None, right=None, eid=None):
        node = len(dag.nodes)
        dag.nodes.append((u, v, length, left, right, eid))
        return node

    # A defined matrix entry is (minimum cost, witness node ID).
    result = matrix()
    for v in range(N):
        result[v][v] = (0, add_node(v, v, 0))

    power = matrix()
    selected = matrix()
    for eid, (u, v, w) in enumerate(E):
        old = selected[u][v]
        if old is None or w < E[old][2]:
            selected[u][v] = eid
    for u in range(N):
        for v in range(N):
            eid = selected[u][v]
            if eid is not None:
                power[u][v] = (
                    E[eid][2], add_node(u, v, 1, eid=eid))
    del selected, E

    def multiply(a, b):
        # Synchronous product: inputs remain unchanged.
        out = matrix()
        for u in range(N):
            for v in range(N):
                best = None
                children = None
                for k in range(N):
                    x, y = a[u][k], b[k][v]
                    if x is None or y is None:
                        continue
                    candidate = x[0] + y[0]
                    if best is None or candidate < best:
                        best = candidate
                        children = (x[1], y[1])
                if children is None:
                    continue
                left, right = children
                ln, rn = dag.nodes[left], dag.nodes[right]
                assert ln[0] == u and ln[1] == rn[0]
                assert rn[1] == v

                    node = right
                elif rn[2] == 0:
                    node = left
                else:
                    node = add_node(
                        u, v, ln[2] + rn[2], left, right)

    while remaining:
        if remaining & 1:
            result = multiply(result, power)
        remaining >>= 1
        if remaining:
            power = multiply(power, power)

    entry = result[S][T]
    if entry is None:
        return ('unreachable', None, None)

    assert status == 'finite' and cost == 0

    assert witness.edge_at(10**18 - 1) == 0

**Exact length and optimal cost.** Define Dₐ[u,v] as the minimum cost of a u→v walk with exactly a edges, or impossible. D₀ is zero only on the diagonal; D₁ selects the cheapest actual edge for each ordered pair. For nonnegative a and b,

At bit position j, `power` represents D₂ʲ and `result` represents Dᵣ for the sum r of selected lower bits. An accumulator multiplication adds 2ʲ to r; squaring doubles the power length. At termination r=L. The identity introduces no extra real edges and no positive-length carries.

**Directed continuity and witness cost.** A leaf is its named directed input edge. An internal node joins a u→k left child to a k→v right child; the matching endpoint establishes continuity. Their edge counts and costs add to the selected matrix entry. An empty child can be omitted because its endpoints coincide and its cost is zero. By induction over creation order, every witness expands to a directed walk with its stored endpoints and length and its matrix cost. Children always predate parents, so the representation is a DAG. The final root therefore represents an S→T walk with exactly L edges and the reported optimum cost.

Parallel edges retain distinct input IDs; ties select the first minimum-weight edge. A negative self-loop is a real one-edge leaf and may be repeated through shared DAG nodes. For L=0, success requires S=T and returns the zero-cost empty witness, regardless of negative cycles. For fixed L there are finitely many edge sequences, so `unbounded` cannot occur. `None` distinguishes impossibility from zero or negative costs.

**Construction time and stored integers.** Let b=L.bit_length()≤60. For L>0 there are b−1 squarings and popcount(L) accumulator products, at most 2b−1 products. Each costs O(N³) deterministic operations and creates at most N² nodes, only after choosing final winners. Including input validation, construction time is O(M+N²+N³b).

The node table contains at most N+N²+N²(2b−1) nodes for L>0, and at most N+N² for L=0. Each stores at most six integers; live matrices store O(N²) costs and node IDs, and validation temporarily stores O(M) integers. Peak storage is therefore O(M+N²(b+1)) stored integers, including the witness. It is not O(L).

Every constructed length is at most L. Costs have magnitude at most L·10¹²≤10³⁰<2¹⁰⁰, so exact Python arithmetic uses a bounded number of integer digits under the supplied limits.

**Indexed retrieval.** At an internal node, compare i with the left length; descend left or subtract that length and descend right. This preserves the desired position in the concatenation. Power witnesses have depth at most b−1, and accumulator concatenations add at most b levels, giving O(b+1) retrieval time and O(1) auxiliary space. Empty witnesses reject every edge index.

Every pairwise squared distance equals one except the squared distance between points zero and one, which equals t. Derive the exact range of t permitting a nondegenerate simplex in d-dimensional Euclidean space, and its squared volume as a function of d and t. A nondegenerate simplex exists exactly when

0 < t < 2d/(d−1).

Its squared d-dimensional volume is

V² = t[2d−(d−1)t] / [2^d(d!)²].

Here is the Gram-matrix proof. Set vᵢ = pᵢ−p₀ for i=1,…,d. The distance identity gives v₁·v₁=t, v₁·vⱼ=t/2 for j≥2, and vᵢ·vⱼ=1/2 for distinct i,j≥2, with diagonal entries 1. Thus, writing n=d−1 and 𝟙 for the n-entry all-ones vector,

G = [[t, (t/2)𝟙ᵀ], [(t/2)𝟙, B]],
B = (Iₙ+𝟙𝟙ᵀ)/2.

B has eigenvalue d/2 along 𝟙 and eigenvalue 1/2 on its orthogonal complement, so it is positive definite. Since B⁻¹𝟙=(2/d)𝟙, the Schur complement is

s = t − (t²/4)𝟙ᵀB⁻¹𝟙
  = t − (d−1)t²/(2d).

Therefore G is positive definite exactly when 0<t<2d/(d−1). Necessity follows because the edge vectors of a nondegenerate Euclidean simplex have a positive-definite Gram matrix. Sufficiency follows by factoring this positive-definite G to obtain d linearly independent Euclidean vectors; their inner products reproduce every prescribed squared distance.

For the volume, det B=d/2^(d−1), hence

det G = det B · s = t[2d−(d−1)t]/2^d,

and V²=det G/(d!)².

Both endpoints are realizable but degenerate. At either endpoint s=0, while B remains positive definite, so G has rank d−1 and the affine dimension is exactly d−1.

• At t=0, p₀=p₁. These are the only coincident points; the remaining d distinct points form a regular (d−1)-simplex.

• At t=2d/(d−1), no points coincide, because every pairwise distance is positive. The Gram matrix implies

p₀+p₁ = [2/(d−1)] Σⱼ₌₂ᵈ pⱼ.

Thus the midpoint of p₀p₁ is the centroid of p₂,…,p_d. Those latter points span a regular (d−2)-simplex, and p₀ and p₁ lie on opposite sides of its affine span, along the perpendicular through its centroid.

Outside the closed endpoint interval, the Schur complement is negative, so G is not positive semidefinite and no Euclidean realization exists.

\frac t2\mathbf1 & B
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\frac12(I_{d-1}+J_{d-1}),
\]

\[
\mathbf1^TB^{-1}\mathbf1=\frac{2(d-1)}d.

\[
\det B=\frac d{2^{d-1}},\qquad
\det G=\det B\,s=\frac{t[2d-(d-1)t]}{2^d}.

**Exact length and optimal cost.** A length-p matrix entry contains the minimum cost among walks using exactly p edges, or `None` for impossibility. Its root represents a walk attaining that cost. The initial power matrix represents one real edge; the identity represents only zero-edge walks between equal vertices. There are no zero-cost carries in positive-length powers.

To multiply length-p and length-q matrices, split every candidate walk after p edges at vertex k. Its cost is at least `ac[i][k] + bc[k][j]`, and optimal halves attain that sum. Minimizing over k therefore gives exactly the length-(p+q) optimum. The recorded concatenation represents those same selected halves. Squaring doubles the power length; accumulator multiplication adds the lengths corresponding to set bits of L. Consequently the final entry represents exactly L real edges and their minimum cost.

**Directed continuity.** Leaves record actual directed input edges. Empty nodes start and end at the same vertex. A concatenation joins an i-to-k child to a k-to-j child, with matching endpoints checked in the code. Induction proves that the represented sequence starts at S, ends at T, is directed and connected, and has the stored length and selected cost. Sharing a child does not eliminate repeated occurrences: a node used twice represents its sequence twice.

**Boundary cases.** When L is zero, success requires S equal to T, with cost zero and an empty witness; every edge index is invalid. Parallel edges retain distinct input IDs, and the cheapest one for each ordered pair is sufficient for the one-edge matrix. A negative self-loop is a real one-edge leaf and may be repeated by the DAG; its fixed-L cost remains finite. `None` denotes impossibility, never a negative-cost sentinel.

**Construction and storage bounds.** Let b = max(1, L.bit_length()), so b is at most 60, and let M be the input edge count. There are at most b accumulator multiplications and b−1 squarings. Each multiplication takes O(N³) deterministic time and creates at most N² nodes, only after selecting each entry's final split. Construction time is O(N + M + N³b), including validation and conversion of the node list to a tuple.

The DAG has at most M initial edge nodes, N empty nodes, and (2b−1)N² concatenation nodes. Each node stores at most five integers; the live cost and root matrices store O(N²) more. Thus peak storage, including the returned DAG, is O(N + M + N²b) stored integers and references—not O(L). Unused initial or intermediate nodes are retained but already included in this bound. Costs have magnitude at most L·10¹² ≤ 10³⁰, and lengths are at most L, so exact Python arithmetic uses bounded-size integers under these limits.

**Retrieval bound.** Squaring increases witness depth by at most one. Each accumulator multiplication also increases depth by at most one, yielding depth at most 2b. Retrieval follows one child per level, subtracting the left length when entering the right child. It therefore takes O(b) time and O(1) additional storage without expansion.
